description: Exact maximum induced edge density by Goldberg's binary-search and min-cut reduction.

source.title: Finding a Maximum Density Subgraph
source.author: A. V. Goldberg
source.copyright: Algorithmic description only; the package is clean-room authored.

input.graph: Simple undirected graph; each edge occurs once with 0 <= u < v < N; edge order is unrestricted; disconnected graphs and isolates are valid.

output.meaning: For reduced maximum density p/q, return p*(N+1)+q; an edgeless graph is encoded as 0/1 and returns 1.

algorithm_details.primary: Binary search g in [0,M] until the interval is strictly narrower than 1/(N*(N-1)). At dyadic midpoint g=a/d, scale Goldberg's min-cut capacities by d: source arcs M*d, both directions of each input edge d, and vertex-to-sink arcs M*d+2*a-d*degree(v). Residual source-side membership determines which bound moves; save each nonempty side. Compute the reduced density of the saved subset.
algorithm_details.independent_oracle: Enumerate every nonempty vertex subset, count its induced edges, and maximize e/|S| by exact integer cross multiplication.
algorithm_details.tie_rules: Edmonds-Karp scans residual neighbors in increasing vertex ID. The minimum source side is the residual-reachable set after max flow. If it contains an input vertex, update the lower bound and save it; otherwise update the upper bound. Exact midpoint ties are valid on either branch.
algorithm_details.termination: Every possible density is e/s with 0<=e<=M and 1<=s<=N; distinct values differ by at least 1/(N*(N-1)). The interval is halved each round, so the strict-width stopping rule identifies an optimal saved subset. M=0 is handled directly as density 0/1.
algorithm_details.arithmetic_bound: At most 11 min-cut calls are needed for N<=8 and M<=28. The dyadic denominator is at most 2048; all scaled capacities and flow residuals fit signed 64-bit integers. The returned encoding is at most 28*(8+1)+8=260.
